Who bills the tax on a Seattle house

King County bills and collects the tax on a Seattle house. The city's own levies ride on the same county statement, so there is no separate city bill. Washington law makes the county treasurer the collector for every district on the roll, whether the levy is for the state, the county, a school district or the city (RCW 84.56.020). The King County Assessor sets the value and publishes the yearly levy sheets that show how Seattle's rate is built.

Seattle counts 784,777 residents (July 1, 2025). Just 43.7% of homes are lived in by their owners, so renters are the majority. Owner-occupied homes had a median value of $938,600 over 2020 to 2024, and households earned a median $123,860.

Seattle's levy code in the King County rate book is 0010. Nearly every parcel inside city limits is in Seattle Public Schools. A small slice of Delridge belongs to the Highline School District instead, which changes the levy lines on the bill.

The 2026 property tax rate

For 2026 the total levy rate for code 0010 is $9.90845 per $1,000 of assessed value, up from $9.19418 in 2025. The King County Assessor's median-home sheet shows a typical Seattle home assessed at $833,000 for 2026 with a tax of $8,253.74. A year earlier the median assessed value was $864,000 and the tax was $7,943.77.

Across the city, the average assessed value changed by negative 3.6%, the average tax rate changed by 7.8% and the average tax changed by 3.9%, or $309.97. Values slipped while rates rose faster, so the average bill went up.

What changed on 2026 bills

Voter-approved levies caused the biggest line changes. Seattle School District 1 passed two special levies, a six-year capital levy and a three-year educational technology levy, and its capital line rose from 1.22694 to 1.41465 per $1,000. The city renewed its six-year families, education, preschool and promise levy and a ten-year election campaign voucher levy. The promise line roughly doubled, from 0.34844 to 0.68956.

King County voters renewed several county measures that appear on every Seattle bill:

  • The automated fingerprint identification system levy, a seven-year renewal.
  • The parks, recreation, trails and open space levy, a six-year renewal.
  • The emergency medical services levy, a six-year renewal, with the EMS line moving from 0.22146 to 0.25098.
  • The county-wide hospital line, which went from 0.10000 to 0.15126.

The city lines for low-income housing, library services and the metro park district stayed close to their 2025 levels. If your bill differs from the median figures above, look at which school district and special districts your parcel sits in.

Due dates and penalties

Your Seattle bill splits into two installments. Half is payable by April 30 and the rest by October 31, a schedule set in RCW 84.56.020. Splitting is open to you only when the bill reaches $50. If the second half is still open after October 31, call the King County treasurer for the current balance.

Late taxes on a residence with four or fewer units accrue interest at 9% a year, computed monthly, and state law bars penalties on those homes. Buildings with five or more units are treated harder: 12% a year, a 3% penalty on June 1, and another 8% penalty on December 1. A treasurer may offer payment agreements or accept partial payments, and can extend due dates during a declared state of emergency.

Your statement should reach you by March 15 when the county has the roll in time. If none arrives, ask the King County treasurer for a copy. Not receiving a bill does not cancel the tax.

How to appeal your assessment

You petition the county board of equalization on forms approved by the Department of Revenue. Your filing window under RCW 84.40.038 closes on whichever comes later: July 1 of the assessment year, or 30 days after your value notice went out by mail or email. The county may adopt a longer period of up to 60 days, so read the deadline printed on your King County valuation notice.

A board can accept a late petition if you file within a reasonable time and show good cause. The statute lists these circumstances:

  • Death or serious illness of the taxpayer or an immediate family member.
  • Absence from your usual address for more than fifteen of the days allowed.
  • Incorrect written filing advice from board or assessor staff.
  • A natural disaster such as a flood or earthquake.
  • A documented postal delay.

The board must also waive the deadline when your area was revalued, your value did not change, and you were never sent a revaluation notice.

Senior and disabled exemption

The state senior and disabled exemption, RCW 84.36.381, can excuse part of the excess and regular levies on your home. You need to own the home and live in it. On top of that, one of three things must be true: you turn 61 by December 31 of the filing year, you stopped regular work because of a disability, or you are a veteran rated 40% or higher for a service-connected condition. A surviving spouse or domestic partner of a recipient can qualify at 57 or older. The amount depends on combined disposable income, so ask the King County Assessor for the current income thresholds.

The exemption can move with you. A claimant who sells, transfers or is displaced may carry the exemption status to a replacement residence, though only one residence per year can receive it. Deferred taxes, a separate program under chapter 84.38 RCW, become a lien repaid to the state with interest when ownership transfers. Tell the assessor about your move before the next filing cycle.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

A tax lien attaches to the house on January 1 of each levy year. If the sale contract says nothing else, RCW 84.60.020 puts the days before closing on you and the days after on the buyer. Escrow normally settles this at closing, along with any unpaid balance or deferral lien. Get a payoff figure from escrow before you sign anything.

Step by step, a sale with taxes owed goes like this. You list or accept an offer. Escrow orders a title report that shows the unpaid balance. The treasurer's office confirms the amount through the closing date. Escrow pays the balance out of your proceeds and prorates the current year. A cash buyer can skip lender appraisal and underwriting delays, which helps when a deferral lien or back taxes need to be cleared on a short timeline.

Real estate excise tax on a sale

Sellers normally cover the state excise tax on the transfer, payable to the county treasurer when the sale closes. The Department of Revenue brackets for sales from January 1, 2027 climb in four steps: 1.1% through $551,000, 1.28% up to $1,551,000, 2.75% up to $3,051,000, then 3%. A local excise tax comes on top. Ask your closing agent what Seattle's local rate is.

Bring these to the closing office: your most recent tax statement, any exemption or deferral paperwork, the sale agreement and a payoff request from your lender. With those in hand, escrow can show you a full settlement sheet before the day of signing.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Seattle property tax rate for 2026?

The total for levy code 0010 is $9.90845 per $1,000 of assessed value. A median home assessed at $833,000 carries about $8,253.74 in tax.

Does the City of Seattle send its own property tax bill?

No. No. One King County statement covers the city, the school district and every other taxing district, and the county treasurer collects it.

What if the second half is still unpaid after October 31?

Call the King County treasurer for the exact balance. Interest on homes with four or fewer units runs 9% a year, figured monthly, with no penalty.

Can I keep my senior exemption if I sell my Seattle house?

Often yes. You can carry the status to a replacement home, one exempt home per year. Tell the assessor about the move.

Who pays property tax at closing in Seattle?

Unless the contract says otherwise, you owe the days before closing and the buyer owes the days after. Escrow does the math and takes any unpaid balance out of your proceeds.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Spokane at a glance

Spokane is the seat of Spokane County, on the Spokane River in eastern Washington, less than 20 miles from the Idaho line. It had 230,783 residents in July 2025, second in the state after Seattle. Fewer city households own their homes than in the county as a whole, so a good share of Spokane houses are rentals when they sell. The 2020 to 2024 numbers for the city and the county:

Housing measureSpokane citySpokane County
Typical home value, owner-occupied$363,500$410,700
Owner-occupied housing rate58.8%64.5%
Median gross rent$1,215$1,283
Households97,446218,395

The school district over a parcel shifts its levy. Spokane Public Schools covers most of the city, and Mead takes the north county beyond the city limits. Pull the parcel record before you quote anybody a number.

Who bills property tax for a Spokane house?

City Hall sends nothing. Property tax in Spokane is billed and collected by the Spokane County Treasurer, with values set by the county Assessor. The City of Spokane is one of roughly 56 taxing districts in the county that hand their budgets to the Assessor each November.

The city's share goes mainly into the General Fund for police, fire, streets, parks and the library. Its proposed 2025 to 2026 budget assumed the 1% increase allowed on regular levies, and it carries a streets levy and a public safety personnel levy fund as dedicated revenue. Other lines on the statement belong to the county, the school district, the state schools and whatever special district covers the lot.

Water, sewer and trash service are paid by fees, not property tax. Before you close, ask the city utility billing office whether the address has an unpaid utility balance.

  • Treasurer's counter: 1116 W. Broadway Ave. in the county courthouse, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. until 4 p.m. Phone 509-477-4713.
  • Assessor: 509-477-3698.
  • For checks in the mail, use the Treasurer's post office box, number 199, zip 99210.

Due dates

Payment comes in a spring half and a fall half, on April 30 and October 31. Small bills, those under $50, come due all at once in April. A date falling on a Saturday, Sunday or county holiday rolls to the next working day. With this fall's half behind you, the next deadline is April 30, 2027.

One statement a year arrives with two coupons. No statement by March 31? Call 509-477-4713 or search SCOUT, the county's online lookup. Escrow customers should check with the lender, because the Treasurer neither bills mortgage companies nor tracks them.

The courthouse has two drop boxes, and they take checks only. Ahead of each deadline the Treasurer sets up outside collection days, two Fridays and two Tuesdays, at Spokane Valley City Hall and the North Spokane Library. Envelopes are judged by federal postmark. Postmarks have been slipping after postal changes, so mail early.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Late interest and penalties

Interest starts May 1 for a missed first half and November 1 for a missed second half, and it runs on the full year's amount. Houses and small residential buildings of up to four units carry 0.75% a month and never a penalty. Other property is charged 1% a month and then takes a 3% penalty on June 1 and 8% on December 1.

State law lets the Treasurer set up payment agreements and accept partial payments on current and past-due taxes, with money going to the oldest year first (RCW 84.56.020). After the death of a spouse, parent or stepparent, a hardship waiver is possible if you give notice within 60 days of the due date (RCW 84.56.025). Interest cannot be waived when the statement went to an address supplied by the taxpayer or the taxpayer's agent, a closing agent for example.

If your bank bounces a payment, add a $30 fee on top of interest, penalty and costs.

How do you challenge a Spokane assessment?

Appeals for a house inside city limits go to the Spokane County Board of Equalization. Use the petition form and file it by July 1 of the assessment year. If your Change of Value Notice was mailed later, you get 30 days from that mailing. Filing costs nothing. Calling or writing a letter does not replace the form.

The board looks only at market value, and the assessor's number is presumed right unless your evidence is clear, cogent and convincing (RCW 84.40.0301). Build your case around these points:

  • Tax amount, percentage increase, other properties' values and personal hardship cannot be considered.
  • Comparable sales close to January 1 of the assessment year make the strongest case.
  • Supporting papers must arrive seven business days before you appear.
  • Notice of the hearing comes 15 business days ahead.

Call the Assessor first at 509-477-3698, since many disagreements end in a stipulated value. Lose at the county level and the State Board of Tax Appeals is next, with 30 calendar days to file. The county revalues every parcel each year and inspects each one at least once in six years.

Homeowner relief

Seniors and people retired because of disability can apply for a property tax exemption through the Spokane County Assessor at 509-477-3698. Senate Bill 6162, signed after the 2026 session, changes the income limits starting in 2027, so ask for the limits that apply to you instead of trusting older numbers.

Every statement is required by RCW 84.56.020 to point to the exemption and the deferral program. An owner who is income-qualified, lives in the home and faces a tax foreclosure action can have interest and penalties waived about three years after delinquency, once per property.

Buyers get a special path too. Someone who bought between July 1 and December 31 of the assessment year for under 90% of assessed value can ask the Board of Equalization to reconvene after the normal deadline.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What should you do about back taxes when selling in Spokane?

Get a payoff letter from the Treasurer that covers each unpaid year, pass it to the closing agent, and check that the agent holds the right parcel number and mailing address. Remember that interest stays in place if the county's statement was mailed to an address the closing agent supplied.

Excise tax on the sale is its own charge, owed to the county treasurer at the moment of sale, and the seller usually covers it. For sales from January 1, 2027, a house at the city's $363,500 median value falls entirely in the 1.1% state bracket, before any local rate is added.

Waiting is risky. At three years past delinquency, the treasurer is required to begin foreclosure by certificate of delinquency (RCW 84.64.050).

Closing checklist for a Spokane seller

A tidy tax file makes a sale move faster. Start a few weeks before you list and work down this list:

  • Pull the parcel record on SCOUT and write down the parcel number, the school district and what each half shows as paid.
  • Ring 509-477-4713 for a written payoff when any earlier year is open.
  • Ask the city utility billing office about any water, sewer or trash balance on the address.
  • Tell the Assessor at 509-477-3698 if a senior or disability exemption or a deferral is attached, so the closing agent knows to plan for it.
  • Give the closing agent a mailing address you actually check, because late-notice mail goes to whatever address is on file.

A cash buyer can often close quickly, and no lender runs its own tax review. The payoff letter is still needed, since any back tax comes out of your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

Where does my Spokane property tax payment go?

To the Spokane County Treasurer, in person on W. Broadway Ave., by mail to P.O. Box 199, or online. The phone is 509-477-4713. City Hall collects none of it.

When is Spokane property tax due?

Twice a year, April 30 and October 31. Under $50 is paid in one lump in April. Next up is April 30, 2027, shifting to the next business day if it is a weekend.

How do I appeal my Spokane property value?

Your appeal goes to the county's equalization board, and the cutoff is July 1, or a month after the value notice went out if that comes later. No fee applies, and you will want market evidence such as nearby sales.

What interest applies to late Spokane property tax?

A house of up to four units pays 0.75% monthly with no penalty. Other property pays 1% monthly and also takes the June and December penalties. Each charge is figured on the whole year's tax.

Can I sell a Spokane house that owes back taxes?

Yes. Whatever is owed gets paid by escrow out of your sale money. Get the payoff from the Spokane County Treasurer and give your closing agent the right parcel number and mailing address.

Vancouver, WA Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Washington
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Vancouver, WA Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Vancouver, WA Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Vancouver, WA Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Owe Vancouver Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Vancouver houses as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Vancouver property tax?
We buy Vancouver houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.

Clark County offices for Vancouver owners

Vancouver houses are taxed by Clark County. The Treasurer, the Assessor and the Board of Equalization all work from the Public Service Center, 1300 Franklin Street, downtown. Values come from the Assessor, statements and payments from the Treasurer, and appeals go before the Board.

  • Treasurer: 564.397.2252, treasoff@clark.wa.gov, second-floor Joint Lobby. Walk-in hours are Monday to Thursday, nine in the morning to four in the afternoon. Phone and email help is offered on Fridays as well, until 4:30 in the afternoon.
  • Assessor: 564.397.2391, assessor@clark.wa.gov.
  • Board of Equalization: Suite 650, 564.397.2337, BOE@clark.wa.gov.

Vancouver housing and city limits

Vancouver is the Clark County seat, on the north bank of the Columbia River across from Portland. It had 199,698 residents in July 2025 on 48.74 square miles of land. Owners occupy 50.8 percent of homes. The median owner-occupied home is worth $462,400, median gross rent is $1,702 and median household income is $81,338.

Not every Vancouver mailing address is inside the city. Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek are unincorporated communities just north of the city limits. The county's Property Information Center will show whether your parcel is in the city, and the levies shift with the tax area.

Vancouver tax rate by district

For 2026 the county's levy report puts the total at $9.6856 per $1,000 of assessed value in tax area 037000, which covers the City of Vancouver and Vancouver School District 37. Other tax areas inside the city carry different district combinations, so trust the rate on your own statement.

The library line combines a general rate of 0.5000 and a capital facilities rate of 0.0948.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Payment deadlines and late charges

Spring brings the first-half deadline, April 30, and that is also the date for anyone paying the full year at once. The fall deadline is October 31. A mailed check counts only if the Postal Service postmarks it that same day, so the county advises handing it to a post office clerk and avoiding the collection box. E-check payments online are free. Expect first-half statements around March 15 and second-half statements around September 15.

For tax years 2023 and later, a residential parcel of four or fewer units is charged 0.75 percent a month and no penalty. Everything else is billed 1 percent monthly and adds a 3 percent penalty on June 1, then 8 percent on December 1.

  • Chapter 84.64 RCW lets the county foreclose on real property once three or more years of tax are unpaid.
  • After court proceedings begin, all taxes, interest, penalties and foreclosure costs must be paid in full before the auction.
  • After a certificate of delinquency is filed, only owners and recorded interests can make payments to the Treasurer.
  • Owner-occupants who qualify by income and face foreclosure may ask once for interest and penalties to be waived under RCW 84.56.020(19).

The Treasurer's office is the right first call for a payoff figure, and nothing about a pending sale stops you from paying a delinquent year early. If you are behind, email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov or call 564.397.2252 before you list the home.

Does your mortgage escrow pay Vancouver property tax?

More than 45 percent of Clark County homeowners pay through escrow. For those owners the county sends no statement, and you stay responsible for confirming each installment was actually paid.

Lenders occasionally pay the wrong account number or skip a payment. After April 30 and October 31, open the taxes tab on the Property Information Center and check. If a delinquency notice shows up, ask the lender which account numbers it paid and request a cancelled check or disbursement record. Confirm with the lender before sending your own money, because paying twice is a real risk.

How to appeal a Vancouver property value

Your window is 60 calendar days from the date printed on the Notice of Value, or July 1 if that comes later, and the appeal goes to the county's equalization board. Late appeals cannot be accepted, and the 60 days are counted from the notice date, not as two months. You may also file a preemptive appeal anytime from January 1 through July 1 of the assessment year.

Most Notices of Value go out in June and the rest in September, and only properties whose value changed receive one. Filing is free. A three-member citizen board hears each case in about 15 minutes and mails a written decision within 30 days. Historically, more than half of appeals end well for the owner, either after a talk with the Assessor or at the hearing.

  • Strongest evidence: comparable sales or a recent appraisal, repair bids and photographs.
  • Other properties' assessed values do not persuade the board.
  • Extra evidence has to reach the Board 21 business days before the hearing.
  • If you disagree with the result, the State Board of Tax Appeals is the next stop.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Senior exemption and closing steps

Clark County's senior exemption uses three income tiers. For tax years 2024 through 2026 the top income limit is $62,000, and for 2027 through 2029 it rises to $85,000 under Senate Bill 6162. Applicants for 2027 need to be 61 or older, unable to work due to disability, or rated 40 percent or higher for a service-connected disability. They must also own the home and occupy it at least six months of the year. Applications for 2027 open in February 2027, and current participants are adjusted automatically.

At closing, RCW 84.60.020 attaches the tax lien on January 1 and, without a contract term, divides the year by the sale date. Ask your escrow officer to confirm both halves with the Treasurer, and ask the Assessor whether an exemption or deferral ends with the sale.

Review the statement before listing

Before you put a Vancouver house on the market, spend ten minutes with the statement. Each bill lists the taxes from every district, and the county's lookup shows whether anything is delinquent.

  • Confirm the tax area number, since it decides the rate.
  • Check both halves as paid, especially if a lender handles escrow.
  • See whether an exemption is on the account, and learn from the Assessor what stops when you sell.
  • If a balance is open, email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov for a payoff before the buyer's title company asks.

With a cash buyer there is no lender reviewing taxes, yet the title company still checks the record and anything owed is taken from your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

When is Vancouver, WA property tax due?

Spring and fall: April 30 covers the first half or the full year, and October 31 covers the second half. Statements are usually ready by March 15 and September 15.

What interest does Clark County charge on late property tax?

A residential parcel of four or fewer units owes 0.75 percent monthly with no penalties, for tax years 2023 and later. Everything else pays 1 percent monthly and picks up the June 1 and December 1 penalties of 3 and 8 percent.

How long before Clark County forecloses for unpaid taxes?

Three years. Real property with taxes three or more years delinquent can be foreclosed. Call the Treasurer at 564.397.2252 or email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov to discuss relief.

What is the appeal window in Vancouver?

Sixty calendar days counted from the mailing date of your Notice of Value, unless July 1 is later. Late appeals cannot be accepted. Reach the Board of Equalization at 564.397.2337 or BOE@clark.wa.gov.

Is my Vancouver address inside city limits?

Not always. Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek sit north of the city limits and are unincorporated. The Clark County Property Information Center shows which tax area applies to your parcel.

Who bills Tacoma homeowners?

Bills come from Pierce County. Tacoma is the county seat, and the county's Assessor-Treasurer's Office values each house and also collects the money.

  • Pay or check a balance in person: Pierce County Annex, 2401 S 35th Street, Room 142, Tacoma. A drop box serves after-hours payments.
  • Customer service: (253) 798-6111.
  • Automated tax and value line: (253) 798-3333. With a parcel number it takes card and e-check payments.
  • Foreclosure avoidance payments: send a cashier's check to Pierce County marked Attention: Foreclosure Avoidance, at the Room 142 address.

The city's own levy is folded into one combined rate. Statements go out in February and the county collects the whole amount.

Tacoma housing snapshot

Tacoma is a port city on Puget Sound, roughly 30 miles from Seattle and from Olympia, with 229,816 residents in July 2025 on 49.71 square miles. Owners occupy 55.8 percent of homes, and the median value of an owned home is $479,600. Median gross rent is $1,676 and median household income is $85,884.

Roughly 44 percent of Tacoma households rent, and that is a fact to weigh before you list. If the house you are selling has a tenant, plan for that in your timeline, because tax bills and sale paperwork still run through you as the owner of record.

Due dates

Owners pay one half by April 30 and the second half by October 31. Statements arrive in February. A bill of $50 or less is paid whole on April 30. A statement that never showed up is no excuse, and interest still builds.

Mail the check so the postmark falls on or before the deadline. The county suggests certified mail with a return receipt, so you hold proof of the mailing date, and it will forgive interest when the postmark shows you mailed in time. If a check comes in late and short on the right interest, it is returned. Lenders live by the same calendar as individual owners and are expected to pay every tax, assessment and charge on the parcel.

The county prints your parcel number, the value used and each district's levy on the statement. Keep that statement with your sale paperwork, since the title company will ask for the parcel number and for proof of what has been paid. If the statement is lost, call the same number for a copy.

What is the Tacoma tax rate?

For 2026, Pierce County puts the average rate in Tacoma's tax code area 005 at $10.876 per $1,000 of assessed value. That single figure covers every taxing district stacked on the area. Individual parcels can drift a little from the average, so read the rate on your own statement.

The assessor looks at sales made before January 1 and values every parcel as of that day. The 2026 assessment therefore reflects 2025 sales, and it forms the base for taxes due in 2027. The county explains the yearly calendar on its residential appeals page.

If you fall behind on Tacoma property tax

For a residential property with one to four units and tax year 2023 or later, interest is 0.75 percent per month on the full year's tax from May 1. Penalties of 3 percent and 8 percent are charged on other property types, so a single-family house does not collect them. Monthly payment plans are offered by the Assessor-Treasurer:

  • A plan for current tax through escrow costs $100 to set up and $15 a month.
  • A plan for delinquent tax costs $100 to set up and $17 a month, and it can run up to 18 months.
  • The oldest unpaid tax has to be cleared in full by April 30 of the year it turns three years delinquent.

Foreclosure comes next. Parcels with more than $100 in cumulative tax that is three or more years delinquent are foreclosed through a Certificate of Delinquency filed in Pierce County Superior Court. To ask about a plan, call (253) 798-2728.

How do you appeal a Tacoma property value?

The Pierce County Board of Equalization takes petitions filed by July 1 or within 60 days after your value change notice was mailed. It accepts only the Department of Revenue petition form, one parcel per form.

  • Hearings turn on what the house was worth on January 1. The size of the bill, a big percentage jump, what neighbors pay and your finances are all off the table.
  • Good evidence includes comparable sales from the right year, contractor bids to fix defects, easement documents, independent appraisals and photographs.
  • A petition that merely says the value or tax is too high is rejected.
  • Late exhibits are due 21 business days ahead of the hearing.

The county's value is presumed correct, which puts the burden of proof on you. The board's office is at 2401 S 35th St, Room 176, phone (253) 798-7415. RCW 84.40.038 sets the baseline deadlines and spells out good-cause reasons for accepting a late petition.

Exemptions and taxes at closing

Seniors and people with disabilities may apply for an exemption that can freeze taxable value and remove certain levies. You qualify if you are at least 61 or have been awarded disability status by December 31 of the previous year, earn no more than $64,000 after allowable deductions, own the home by December 31 of the assessment year, and live in it more than six months of the prior year. An application is required.

Excise tax on the sale is billed apart from property tax. The state rate climbs with the price:

These are the rates for sales on or after January 1, 2023, and Tacoma adds a 0.50 percent local rate. Property tax itself is prorated by sale date under RCW 84.60.020, with the lien attaching each January 1. Have your escrow officer confirm the open half with the Assessor-Treasurer.

Steps for a Tacoma seller

Do this homework before the listing goes live so tax questions do not stall escrow.

  • Look up the parcel number and check what the automated line at (253) 798-3333 shows as owed.
  • Check whether the fall half is paid, and if not, get the exact interest to date.
  • If you are on a payment plan, tell escrow so the remaining balance is cleared from proceeds.
  • If you hold a senior or disability exemption, confirm with the Assessor-Treasurer what changes when ownership transfers.
  • If a tenant lives in the house, work out the showing schedule before you list.

Sellers who need a fast close sometimes choose a cash buyer, which skips the appraisal and lender review. Any tax owed still comes out of the proceeds, so you need the payoff number regardless of who buys.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I pay Tacoma property tax to?

Pierce County's Assessor-Treasurer, not the city. Options are the website, the phone line at (253) 798-3333, a mailed check to Pierce County Finance, or the counter at 2401 S 35th Street, Room 142. Checks are made out to Pierce County.

What is the interest on late Tacoma property tax?

On a home of four or fewer units, 0.75 percent a month on the full year's tax from May 1, for tax year 2023 and later. The 3 and 8 percent penalties apply to other property types.

How long can Tacoma property tax go unpaid before foreclosure?

Three years. Pierce County forecloses on parcels with more than $100 in cumulative tax that is three or more years delinquent.

When must I file a Tacoma assessment appeal?

The county board wants your petition by July 1 of the assessment year, or 60 days after your value change notice was mailed. Attach a copy of that notice if you file after July 1.

Is there excise tax on a Tacoma home sale?

Yes. The state graduated excise rate applies to the sale, and Tacoma adds a 0.50 percent local rate. Your escrow officer can give the exact figure at your sale price.
